summary: w-screenctl exposes unauthenticated remote host-control server on 0.0.0.0:7000
details: On startup, w-screenctl launches a Hapi HTTP server bound to 0.0.0.0:7000 with CORS enabled and no authentication. The server exposes endpoints that hand HTTP request bodies directly to host-control sinks: /chrome/evaluate forwards a caller-supplied 'script' string to Playwright page.evaluate (arbitrary JavaScript execution inside the controlled browser), and /keyboard/key and /keyboard/type route arbitrary keystrokes into the host desktop session via xdotool/w-mousekey. Additional endpoints provide mouse control and full-screen capture. Because the listener binds to all interfaces with no credential check, any peer able to reach TCP/7000 on the host — LAN, VPN, or exposed public interface — can drive the desktop, inject keystrokes into any focused window, and thereby spawn a shell or execute arbitrary code on the machine running the package. Screen capture over the same channel enables passive observation of on-screen content including credentials.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
